title: refactor(warehouse): move warehouse-owned code out of core
body:
## Problem

Four modules under `posthog/` were warehouse_sources logic that happened to live in core.
Each one had to import back across the product boundary to reach the models it operates on, so code that belongs to one product showed up as core depending on that product.

Third layer of the stack under #82442 and #83035.

## Changes

- The column-validation celery task moves into the product. It reads a table, calls the model's own `validate_column_type`, and saves, with no core concern in it.
- Its celery name is pinned to the old dotted path. Moving a `@shared_task` renames it, which would strand any message queued before the deploy.
- The activity-log detail helpers move into the product. Their only caller was the product's own `activity_logging` module.
- Two management commands move into the product. Django discovers commands per app, so `reenable_schemas_by_error` and `sync_import_pipeline_schedules` are invoked exactly as before.
- Tests move with their subjects, including the `@patch` targets that named the old module paths.
- `data_warehouse` reaches the relocated task through `facade/tasks.py`, the existing wiring submodule for celery tasks.

## How did you test this code?

- The relocated task and command tests pass in their new locations.
- The task is still registered in celery under its pinned name, checked against the live app registry after `django.setup()`.
- `lint-imports`, `tach check`, and `hogli product:lint --all` pass.
- Not checked: no deploy-time verification that an in-flight message routes. The pinned name is asserted against the registry instead.

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?
- [ ] Alert Sales and Marketing teams?

## Docs update

None. No user-facing behavior, config, or documented workflow changes.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

Written by Claude (Claude Code), directed by Julian. Skills invoked: `/isolating-product-facade-contracts`, `/stacking-prs`, `/writing-tests`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`.

These four came out of the same consumer audit as #83035. They are the group where the fix is relocation rather than a contract: nothing about them needs to cross a boundary once they sit in the product that owns them.

title: chore: clean up feature flag dashboards-list-view after experiment 379125
body:
## Problem

- People browsing dashboards keep the flat list they already see. Experiment 379125 ("Dashboards list view: tree panel vs flat list") tested a folder-tree panel against that list and lost, so the treatment is being removed.
- The `dashboards-list-view` flag and its `tree` arm stayed in the codebase as dead scaffolding after the experiment concluded.

## Changes

- Removed the `DASHBOARDS_LIST_VIEW` flag and the resolver that mapped its variants to an arm.
- The dashboards scene now renders `DashboardsTableContainer` directly instead of the flag-routing wrapper.
- Deleted the `tree` arm: `DashboardsTree`, `DashboardsTreeFolderMenu`, and the `dashboardsFileSystemLogic`/`dashboardsFileSystemUtils` that only mounted in that arm.
- Removed the experiment-only analytics events (`dashboard moved to folder`, `dashboard list searched`, `dashboards tree folder navigated`) and their call sites, keeping the underlying move and search behavior.
- Removed the tree-only bulk "Move to folder" button from the table; the control per-row "Move to another folder" action stays.
- No visible change for users on the control arm, which is the flat table they already had.

## How did you test this code?

- `pnpm --filter=@posthog/frontend fix` (oxlint + oxfmt): clean.
- Jest on the two suites that referenced the removed instrumentation, both pass: `dashboardsLogic.test.ts`, `projectTreeDataLogic.test.ts`.
- Full `typescript:check` reports errors only in unrelated `@posthog/quill` files that fail to resolve because that workspace is not built in this sandbox; none of the files in this diff report errors.
- Not run: the app end to end, since this is a pure removal of a flag-gated path.

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?

## Docs update

None. No user-facing docs referenced the experiment or flag.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Fully autonomous

- I (actually Claude, via PostHog Code) removed the `dashboards-list-view` flag scaffolding end to end: found every reference, kept the `control` code path, and deleted the `tree` arm plus the code that only that arm reached.
- Skills invoked: `/writing-pr-descriptions`.
- Decision worth noting: `reportDashboardMoveInitiated` and the per-row "Move to another folder" action are baseline control behavior (no experiment-cleanup marker, reachable in control via the sidebar entry store), so I kept them; only the tree-only bulk move and the three experiment metric events were removed.

title: fix(postgres): treat a blank stored incremental watermark as no watermark
body:
## Problem

Postgres data warehouse imports can crash mid-sync with `InvalidTextRepresentation: invalid input syntax for type numeric: ""`, surfaced by [error tracking](https://us.posthog.com/project/2/error_tracking/01a011f4-3aac-7ed2-83ef-0ddb36afdf9f).

- The schema's stored incremental watermark (`incremental_field_last_value`) can end up as an empty string instead of `None` or a real value.
- The Postgres source builds a `WHERE column > <watermark>` clause and only falls back to a type-appropriate initial value when the watermark is `None` — an empty string skips that fallback and becomes a literal `''`.
- Postgres rejects comparing `''` against a numeric (or date/timestamp) column, so the query fails instead of falling back like a genuinely missing watermark would.
- The failure surfaces during the row read (`get_rows` / `fetchmany`) rather than the earlier best-effort row-count query, because that query already swallows and logs errors instead of raising.

## Changes

- Guard the three places under `sources/postgres/` that turn a stored watermark into SQL: `_build_query`, `_build_count_query` (`postgres.py`), and `build_partition_query` (`partitioned_tables.py`). An empty-string watermark now falls back to `incremental_type_to_initial_value(...)`, same as `None`.
- Apply the same guard to the windowed and per-partition iterators (`iterate_date_windows`, `iterate_partitions`) before they compare the watermark against typed partition bounds, so a blank value can't reach a `<`/`<=` comparison against a date or number either.

## How did you test this code?

- Added regression tests for `_build_query`, `_build_count_query`, and `build_partition_query`, each asserting an empty-string watermark falls back to the type's initial value (`0`) instead of an empty literal (`''`). These catch the exact query shape that produced the reported error.
- Ran `products/warehouse_sources/backend/temporal/data_imports/sources/postgres/test_postgres.py`: 610 passed, including the new cases. 56 unrelated tests errored because this sandbox has no live Postgres instance for the DB-backed cases; not caused by this change.
- Ran `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` on the changed files: clean.
- Not run: mypy, and manual reproduction against a live source (no test Postgres instance available here).

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?

## Docs update

None — internal query-building fix, no user-facing or documented behavior changes.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Fully autonomous

Triaged a production error tracking issue and traced it to a stored `""` incremental watermark reaching a SQL literal comparison against a numeric column. Used the PostHog MCP error-tracking tools to pull the issue and a sample stack trace, then read the Postgres source's query-building code to find every place the watermark reaches a literal or a typed comparison. Invoked `/writing-tests` before adding the regression tests and `/writing-pr-descriptions` before writing this body. No duplicate open PR (human-authored) addresses this; searched by exception type, message, and module path.

title: fix(cli): delete CSS source maps after upload
body:
## Problem

Next.js builds that use `deleteAfterUpload` still publish CSS source maps and their `sourceMappingURL` comments. The CLI only includes JavaScript pairs in its cleanup list.

Closes PostHog/posthog-js#4546

## Changes

- Find CSS source-map pairs after the JavaScript upload succeeds.
- Resolve stdin paths once and reuse them for JavaScript upload and CSS cleanup.
- Parse CSS comments separately from JavaScript and ignore comment-like text inside CSS strings.
- Remove only the CSS source-map directive while preserving adjacent license comments and other content.
- Delete CSS maps only when their canonical paths remain inside a selected output root.
- Skip traversing paths and symlinks that resolve outside selected output roots.
- Keep CSS files out of the symbol-set upload.
- Add a patch changeset for `posthog-cli`.
- Add tests for CSS comments, quoted and continued strings, adjacent licenses, pair discovery, path containment, traversal, and symlinks.

## How did you test this code?

- `cargo test --manifest-path cli/Cargo.toml --lib`
- `cargo test --manifest-path cli/Cargo.toml --test sourcemap`
- `cargo clippy --manifest-path cli/Cargo.toml --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt --manifest-path cli/Cargo.toml -- --check`

I did not run a live source-map upload because it requires project credentials and would create remote data.

👉 _Stay up-to-date with [PostHog coding conventions](https://posthog.com/docs/contribute/coding-conventions) for a smoother review._

## Automatic notifications

- [x] Publish to changelog?

## Docs update

No documentation change is needed. This restores the existing `deleteAfterUpload` behavior for CSS artifacts.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

Pi implemented and reviewed this focused fix under human direction. The investigation, Karpathy guidelines, PR, address-pr-comments, and autoreview skills were used. Review feedback led to single-pass stdin resolution, path containment, and CSS-aware comment parsing that preserves adjacent and quoted content. The final review found no actionable issues.

title: chore(devex): make product isolation checks enforce what they claim
body:
## Problem

Every warehouse_sources backend change runs the full Django suite fan-out since #71486 deleted the product's turbo.json. About 70% of the ~830 commits that touched the product since would have skipped it under the old narrowing.

The deletion was correct at the time: the facade handed out classes from `backend/types.py` and a test mixin from `backend/tests/`, neither watched by the old inputs, so a change there could skip the suite. But the lint had no vocabulary for the sound part of the old config, which watched `backend/models/**` alongside the model classes the facade hands out. Core HogQL reads those models at query time to build warehouse tables, so they cannot stop crossing yet.

While restoring it, two more gaps turned up in the enforcement itself, so this PR is really one thing: make the isolation checks enforce what they claim.

grimp builds its import graph from `products`, which is a regular package — it carries an `__init__.py` so file-based mypy resolves `products.<name>.backend` rather than `<name>.backend` (#36780). From a regular package grimp does not descend into PEP 420 namespace sub-directories, and it stops at the first directory without a marker. Eleven products were missing one, so 193 modules were absent from the graph, and `presentation must use facade` was reporting success for code it could not read.

Context: #team-warehouse-sources asked whether the deletion was intentional and how to get isolated CI back.

## Changes

- warehouse_sources gets its narrowed contract-check inputs back, so changes to source connectors and other unwatched internals skip the full suite again.
- A new watched-models allowance in the isolation lint sanctions what the old config did: a facade may hand out Django model classes defined under `backend/models/` if `backend/models/` and `backend/migrations/` stay in the contract-check inputs. Same soundness contract as wiring locations: a model or migration change still re-runs the full suite.
- The allowance (`MODEL_CROSSINGS`) is keyed `(product, class)`, like the carve-outs above it. An unlisted class is a leak again and blocks narrowing, so a listed product cannot grow a new crossing without a doctrine amendment. The list only shrinks.
- `products/architecture.md` now states the bar for an entry: some consumer needs ORM semantics a contract cannot express, such as relation traversal, queryset-typed access-control filtering, row locking, or model behavior. A consumer that only reads fields, or ends in `values_list`, is disqualifying and gets a facade function instead.
- The lint keeps a standing warning on every crossing so the debt stays visible. It groups by class, so the count matches the sanctioned list rather than double-counting classes both facade modules re-export.
- Three re-exports turned out to be dead and are dropped rather than sanctioned. `PendingSourceCredential` and `CustomOAuth2Integration` have no consumers. `SSHTunnel` had one: a test for a warehouse_sources model parked in data_warehouse, now moved into the product, where it imports the model directly and needs no facade.
- The two real holes are fixed by moving the definitions into the facade, where the inputs always watch them: the shared type surface (`backend/types.py`, mostly the source-type enum) moves to `facade/types.py` with a re-export shim behind it, and the access-control test mixin moves into `facade/testing.py`.
- Seven test files in other products imported the mixin's internal module directly; they now go through the facade.
- The restored turbo.json keeps the old test-dir exclusions and adds `backend/presentation/**`, `backend/routes.py`, `backend/migrations/**`, and the two `temporal/` files the model package imports.
- 23 package markers make every product backend visible to import-linter, and a `product:lint` check keeps them there. Test directories and generated trees stay namespace packages: no contract targets them, and marking them would mean thousands of pointless files.
- The markers surfaced 33 real violations. Five are fixed here. stamphog's webhooks reach its tasks through `facade/tasks`, its views reach the GitHub client through a new `facade/github`, `StamphogGitHubError` moves to contracts where error types belong, and data_catalog's serializer takes its length limit from the facade.
- stamphog's presentation moves off `ModelViewSet`/`ModelSerializer` onto `GenericViewSet` plus `DataclassSerializer` over the DTOs its facade already defined. A `ModelViewSet` needs the ORM class in presentation, which is what made the product's own models cross its facade, so converting is the only way to close it rather than record it. Its repo-config claim guard, disable-tombstone semantics, run supersession, and installation sync all move behind the facade unchanged. It keeps `backend:contract-check` with no exemptions.
- Writes get dedicated input serializers, since the contracts are output shapes carrying a required id that a create request cannot supply. Public schema component names are pinned so the DTOs do not rename published API types.
- experiments' 28 violations are recorded as `ignore_imports`. They are newly surfaced rather than new: experiments is not isolated, so nothing was ever skipped on their account, and the entries block it from ever adding `backend:contract-check` until they are cleared.
- `AGENTS.md`'s "no empty `__init__.py`" rule gains the matching exception, since the repo's own package roots have always contradicted it.

> [!NOTE]
> The type-surface move is ~1,300 lines of the diff but purely mechanical (the source-type enum relocating), and the 23 markers are empty files. The code to review is `tools/hogli-commands/hogli_commands/product/{isolation,checks}.py`, the doctrine amendment in `products/architecture.md`, and stamphog's presentation conversion — that last one touches documented security invariants, so it is worth reading against `products/stamphog/CLAUDE.md`.

## How did you test this code?

- New hogli-commands tests cover the regressions nothing else catches: a listed class re-export silently re-arming the leak block (narrowing forfeits), an unlisted class on a listed product getting a free pass (the rot vector), a non-allowlisted product getting the same free pass (unsound skip), the allowance leaking beyond `backend/models/`, an unwatched model surface on a narrowed product, and the restored input set not registering as narrowed (skip inert forever).
- `hogli product:lint --all` passes for all 72 products; warehouse_sources shows the standing allowance warning and no issues.
- `test_ci_core_coupled_sources.py` (the guard that resolves core's facade consumption to source vendors and checks input coverage) passes against the restored turbo.json.
- `tach check`, `lint-imports`, ruff, repo-wide mypy, and a DB-backed access-control test through the moved mixin all pass.
- stamphog's full suite passes (243 tests), including the sync-installation, claim-guard, tombstone, and output-allowlist cases that cover the invariants the conversion moved.
- The frontend typechecks with no stamphog errors, and `build:openapi` regenerates clean with every public type name preserved.
- The unwatched-garages gate caught a live omission during the master merge: `backend/tasks/` appeared in the product meanwhile, and the lint refused the restored inputs until it was watched.
- Not checked: an end-to-end turbo-discover run in CI; the narrowing recognition is asserted at the lint layer.

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?
- [ ] Alert Sales and Marketing teams?

## Docs update

`products/architecture.md` § Wiring couplings and `.claude/rules/product-isolation.md` are amended in this PR.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

Written by Claude (Claude Code), directed by Julian throughout, following the design discussion in the Slack thread above. Skills invoked: `/writing-tests`, `/simplify` (four-angle review applied to the diff), `/isolating-product-facade-contracts`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`. The allowance deliberately mirrors the existing carve-out and garage mechanisms in `isolation.py` rather than adding a parallel one; the known transitivity caveat (a model method calling unwatched internals) is the same one garages already accept, and the model package's out-of-package imports are all watched (two `temporal/` files added to the inputs for that).

The first version keyed the allowance by product name. A design review flagged that as the Packwerk `app/public` failure mode, since a listed product could then grow crossings unreviewed, and the per-class rewrite came out of that. The same review audited every consumer of the crossing classes and found most of them migratable: roughly 35 of ~75 production files read only fields or end in `values_list`, so a facade function returning contracts would delete the import. Those migrations are follow-up PRs, not this one, which restores CI and fixes the gate. The residue that survives them is the HogQL database builder, which builds a per-team query database from prefetched querysets on the request path, and the direct-SQL path, whose payload is an encrypted credentials field deliberately kept out of the contracts.
